CONTENT: 00 - Establish the release baseline
DESCRIPTION: Exit gate: the source, production branch, recovery copies and target architecture are agreed.

CONTENT: [P00-01] Preserve current work and take recovery copies
DESCRIPTION: After: Start here. Done when: Review the dirty working tree, commit intended code explicitly, and privately back up environment files, the current database, uploaded files and image metadata. Never commit secrets or discard unrelated changes.

CONTENT: [P00-02] Inventory the existing installation
DESCRIPTION: After: P00-01. Done when: Record DSM and Container Manager versions, NAS CPU/RAM/free disk, MongoDB image/version and volume paths, database/collection names, Auth0 tenant, DNS, backup destinations and current users. Record where the app actually runs today.

CONTENT: [P00-03] Reconcile dev, main and master once
DESCRIPTION: After: P00-02. Done when: Fetch remote refs, inspect history and actual deployed SHA, and choose main as the single production branch unless existing deployment requires a documented alternative. Merge reviewed work without resetting histories; retire master only after updating every consumer.

CONTENT: [P00-04] Choose providers and a monthly spending limit
DESCRIPTION: After: P00-03. Done when: Evaluate MongoDB Atlas, Render Docker hosting and compatible object storage as the proposed cloud stack. Confirm region, backups, outbound networking, cron/browser support, account ownership and monthly cost before provisioning paid services.

CONTENT: [P00-05] Define production access and publication policy
DESCRIPTION: After: P00-04. Done when: NAS stays LAN/VPN-only. Friends initially use private access; public access begins only at the cloud launch gate. Define guest, account and editor permissions, which games/content may be published, and who can approve publication.

CONTENT: [P00-06] Set launch scope and recovery targets
DESCRIPTION: After: P00-05. Done when: Choose ready games/features, supported browsers, expected initial users, proposed RPO of 24 hours and RTO of 2 hours, and an acceptable maintenance window. Adjust these targets explicitly to match backup cost and restore evidence.

CONTENT: [P00-07] Record the release architecture and environment contract
DESCRIPTION: After: P00-06. Done when: Agree on one same-origin Angular-plus-API application image, a separate parser image, persistent media, secret storage and one active parser scheduler. Record NAS/public origins and required variables without values containing secrets.

CONTENT: [P00-08] GATE - approve the baseline and rollout sequence
DESCRIPTION: After: P00-07. Done when: Confirm recovery copies are usable, production branch is unambiguous, provider/budget decisions have owners, and phases use one production environment at a time plus disposable CI services.

CONTENT: 01 - Permissioned games, content and navigation
DESCRIPTION: Exit gate: restricted content cannot be read through the UI, API, search or media URLs.

CONTENT: [P01-01] Design visibility fields and inheritance
DESCRIPTION: After: P00-08. Done when: Add public/editors visibility to game and supported shared-content contracts. Effective visibility must honor every parent; feature flags and archived state remain separate. Newly created content defaults to editors until explicitly published.

CONTENT: [P01-02] Back up and migrate existing visibility safely
DESCRIPTION: After: P01-01. Done when: Inventory existing visibility expectations, back up affected collections, migrate idempotently and preserve IDs, references and account completion. Review existing public items before retaining their public status; do not silently delete data.

CONTENT: [P01-03] Enforce visibility in middleware reads and writes
DESCRIPTION: After: P01-02. Done when: Apply authorization before serialization to lists, individual records, game documents, events, character/story references and protected writes. Return consistent denied/not-found behavior without leaking hidden names or counts.

CONTENT: [P01-04] Protect search, relationships and image access
DESCRIPTION: After: P01-03. Done when: Apply the same policy to search suggestions, linked requirements, media, thumbnails, bulk responses and downloads. Restricted objects must not remain accessible from public object-storage URLs or a static assets directory.

CONTENT: [P01-05] Add editor publication controls
DESCRIPTION: After: P01-04. Done when: Add visible editor-only controls for game/content visibility and show effective inherited restrictions. Explain why a child cannot be public beneath a restricted parent; record publication changes in an audit trail.

CONTENT: [P01-06] Improve switching and navigation between games
DESCRIPTION: After: P01-05. Done when: Show only authorized games and enabled features in the expanded game switcher. Preserve useful per-game context, favorites and recent selections; support keyboard search and provide a valid fallback when the current game becomes inaccessible.

CONTENT: [P01-07] Handle denied deep links and account changes
DESCRIPTION: After: P01-06. Done when: Recheck access for direct URLs, hashes, sign-in/out and editor-role changes. Clear or partition user-dependent caches so a previous editor's hidden content cannot appear for a guest on the same browser.

CONTENT: [P01-08] Add permission and navigation regression coverage
DESCRIPTION: After: P01-07. Done when: Test guest/account/editor access across API endpoints and media, crafted IDs, hidden parent/public child combinations, reference resolution, game switching and two accounts. Existing user progress must survive becoming temporarily inaccessible.

CONTENT: [P01-09] GATE - approve permissioned browsing
DESCRIPTION: After: P01-08. Done when: Demonstrate that an editor sees a restricted game/content while a normal friend and guest cannot retrieve it directly or indirectly. Verify the allowed game's enabled navigation and completion still work.

CONTENT: 02 - Changelog, feedback and release identity
DESCRIPTION: Exit gate: reviewers can identify the deployed version and submit actionable private feedback.

CONTENT: [P02-01] Establish one canonical changelog
DESCRIPTION: After: P01-09. Done when: Preserve CHANGLOG.md history while correcting the filename to CHANGELOG.md and updating references. Verify the future-dated 2026-11-26 entry; place unreleased changes under Unreleased rather than inventing a release date.

CONTENT: [P02-02] Expose a safe application version
DESCRIPTION: After: P02-01. Done when: Display release version and short commit SHA in About/settings and feedback context. Generate these from the tested build; do not expose environment variables or deployment credentials.

CONTENT: [P02-03] Add the in-app changelog
DESCRIPTION: After: P02-02. Done when: Show reviewed user-facing release notes with dates and feature summaries. Keep internal-only games, hidden content and security-sensitive details out of public notes; link notes to the release SHA.

CONTENT: [P02-04] Implement a feedback intake and editor inbox
DESCRIPTION: After: P02-03. Done when: Add bug, usability and feature-request categories, optional contact, route/game context and version. Keep submissions private, validate lengths, rate-limit intake and authorize inbox access on the server.

CONTENT: [P02-05] Add consent and safe diagnostics
DESCRIPTION: After: P02-04. Done when: Let users review diagnostics and explicitly opt into screenshots/contact information. Never attach access tokens, refresh tokens, cookies, database URLs or unrelated account data. Define retention and deletion behavior.

CONTENT: [P02-06] Support feedback triage and resolution
DESCRIPTION: After: P02-05. Done when: Track new, accepted, in-progress and resolved feedback with severity, reproduction steps and a link to the eventual fix/release. Choose an owner and avoid duplicating private submissions into public issues automatically.

CONTENT: [P02-07] Test feedback and release-note access
DESCRIPTION: After: P02-06. Done when: Verify logged-out and signed-in flows, denied inbox access, malformed/spam submissions, safe error states and keyboard/mobile behavior. Confirm a failed submission preserves the user's text.

CONTENT: [P02-08] GATE - approve the reviewer support loop
DESCRIPTION: After: P02-07. Done when: A normal reviewer can find the running version, submit a private report and receive a clear acknowledgement; an editor can triage it and document its resolution.

CONTENT: 03 - Build pipeline, tests and security gates
DESCRIPTION: Exit gate: a single trustworthy result describes all required checks for the exact candidate SHA.

CONTENT: [P03-01] Audit the two current CI workflows
DESCRIPTION: After: P00-08. Done when: Review ci.yml, browser-integration.yml and CodeRabbit configuration. Record actual required check names, branch rules, permissions and timeouts; distinguish configuration present in Git from settings actually enabled on GitHub.

CONTENT: [P03-02] Pin a consistent toolchain
DESCRIPTION: After: P03-01. Done when: Use .node-version and a deliberate npm version across developer, CI and image builds. Pin reviewed action versions/SHAs and container bases; reconcile current checkout/setup-node v4 versus v6 usage without blind major upgrades.

CONTENT: [P03-03] Run all existing quality commands on clean installs
DESCRIPTION: After: P03-02. Done when: Require npm ci, npm run lint:ci, npm test and npm run ui:build. Fix errors and deliberately ratchet warnings; keep broad formatting cleanup separate. Save commands and results against the candidate SHA.

CONTENT: [P03-04] Keep browser integration a required check
DESCRIPTION: After: P03-03. Done when: Run npm run parser:browser-test and npm run ui:e2e on Ubuntu with disposable MongoDB and installed Playwright libraries. Verify auth, account isolation, persistence, concurrent updates, uploads, logout and cleanup; no production DB or Auth0 bypass.

CONTENT: [P03-05] Expand deployment-related regression coverage
DESCRIPTION: After: P03-04. Done when: Add visibility, enabled-feature navigation, private images, changelog/feedback and direct-link cases. Validate auth and refresh recovery without weakening production JWT verification. Add readiness and deployed-image smoke checks when packaging exists.

CONTENT: [P03-06] Add dependency, secret and container scanning
DESCRIPTION: After: P03-05. Done when: Scan commits/dependencies and later built images; set an explicit policy for actionable high/critical issues with time-limited documented exceptions. Add an update bot and lockfile review. Ensure scanner failures cannot silently pass.

CONTENT: [P03-07] Make code review enforceable and practical
DESCRIPTION: After: P03-06. Done when: Confirm CodeRabbit runs on relevant PRs, resolve actionable findings, and choose supported blocking checks or an explicit release-review policy. Do not require an unavailable second human for every solo-authored PR or assume comments equal approval.

CONTENT: [P03-08] Create an aggregate release-readiness check
DESCRIPTION: After: P03-07. Done when: One stable required check must fail when lint, tests, build, browser integration or mandatory security/review checks fail, cancel or skip. It must evaluate the same candidate commit, not the last successful run on a branch.

CONTENT: [P03-09] Harden workflow credentials and artifacts
DESCRIPTION: After: P03-08. Done when: Untrusted PRs receive no deployment secrets and never execute on the NAS. Use least-privilege workflow tokens, safe checkout, bounded artifact retention and redacted failure diagnostics; do not execute PR code through privileged pull_request_target jobs.

CONTENT: [P03-10] GATE - demonstrate passing and failing candidates
DESCRIPTION: After: P03-09. Done when: Show a complete green candidate and intentionally failing/cancelled checks that block promotion. Verify a subsequent push invalidates old success, and document the exact required checks and measured runtime.

CONTENT: 04 - Automatic dev-to-main promotion
DESCRIPTION: Exit gate: dev is merged automatically through a protected PR only after all required checks pass.

CONTENT: [P04-01] Configure production branch protections
DESCRIPTION: After: P03-10. Done when: Protect main against force pushes, deletion and direct writes; require current checks and an up-to-date merge candidate. Verify GitHub plan support for these protections and auto-merge. AI-authored changes use the same policy.

CONTENT: [P04-02] Choose a promotion merge strategy
DESCRIPTION: After: P04-01. Done when: Use merge commits for recurring dev-to-main promotion so long-lived branch ancestry stays coherent. Short-lived feature branches may use squash. Document conflict resolution and how any main hotfix returns to dev.

CONTENT: [P04-03] Create or update one dev-to-main promotion PR
DESCRIPTION: After: P04-02. Done when: After dev's aggregate check succeeds, automation updates one same-repository PR with head dev and base main. Include changelog/test evidence and deduplicate retries; revalidate the current SHA before taking action.

CONTENT: [P04-04] Configure a scoped automation identity
DESCRIPTION: After: P04-03. Done when: Use a minimally privileged GitHub App where needed for unattended PR/check/merge events. Verify the actual event chain: GITHUB_TOKEN-created PR checks can require approval and token-driven pushes may not start later workflows. Avoid a broad personal token.

CONTENT: [P04-05] Enable protected auto-merge
DESCRIPTION: After: P04-04. Done when: Enable auto-merge for the approved promotion PR; allow required checks and review policy to decide readiness. Never use administrator bypass or force a merge after only unit tests pass. New pushes must rerun checks.

CONTENT: [P04-06] Verify the merged main commit before publishing
DESCRIPTION: After: P04-05. Done when: Run the complete required suite for the resulting main commit, then authorize artifact publication for that SHA. Prove the chosen merge identity triggers the main workflow; otherwise dispatch and verify it explicitly.

CONTENT: [P04-07] Handle conflicts, stale results and emergency holds
DESCRIPTION: After: P04-06. Done when: Notify on conflicts, failed review, cancelled runs and protected-branch failures. Add a release hold/kill switch; do not auto-resolve conflicts or promote an old green SHA after dev advances.

CONTENT: [P04-08] GATE - rehearse two promotions and a blocked merge
DESCRIPTION: After: P04-07. Done when: Demonstrate two successive dev-to-main merges, an intentionally failing PR, a new-commit rerun and a main hotfix reconciliation. Confirm unrelated branches/forks cannot trigger promotion.

CONTENT: 05 - Production packaging and persistent storage
DESCRIPTION: Exit gate: the tested app and parser images run without the checkout or developer machine.

CONTENT: [P05-01] Add an explicit production runtime
DESCRIPTION: After: P04-08. Done when: Create a production start command without ng serve, --watch or the local database launcher. Bundle/compile the API with working @lib/@common resolution and runtime dependencies; do not assume tsc rewrites import aliases.

CONTENT: [P05-02] Make the application host and port configurable
DESCRIPTION: After: P05-01. Done when: Replace the hard-coded API bind to 127.0.0.1 with configuration: keep a safe local-development default and bind 0.0.0.0 inside the production container. Honor the cloud PORT contract while keeping database ports private.

CONTENT: [P05-03] Serve the Angular build and API from one origin
DESCRIPTION: After: P05-02. Done when: Add production static serving with safe paths, correct MIME/cache headers and SPA deep-link fallback. API 404s must remain JSON rather than index.html; protected uploads must never be exposed through static fallback.

CONTENT: [P05-04] Externalize public Auth0 and origin configuration
DESCRIPTION: After: P05-03. Done when: Support NAS and cloud origins without embedding environment-specific values in the immutable image. Provide only non-secret SPA configuration; preserve server issuer/audience/client validation and exact allowed origins.

CONTENT: [P05-05] Move uploaded media out of the source tree
DESCRIPTION: After: P05-04. Done when: Replace the current source-assets imageRoot with configurable persistent storage. Migrate files and JSON metadata with checksums, retain existing /api/games/.../images URLs and support bundled legacy assets during migration.

CONTENT: [P05-06] Add a storage adapter suitable for cloud hosting
DESCRIPTION: After: P05-05. Done when: Provide an object-storage implementation or equivalent durable cloud storage. Preserve metadata, attribution, authorization and deletion rules; restricted media stays private with authorized delivery. Test lost-upload/retry and restore behavior.

CONTENT: [P05-07] Build a minimal non-root application image
DESCRIPTION: After: P05-06. Done when: Add a multi-stage Dockerfile and .dockerignore excluding .env, Git, databases, uploads, tmp and credentials. Include only required runtime dependencies, graceful shutdown and health checks; verify amd64 on the DS1522+.

CONTENT: [P05-08] Harden and test the existing parser image
DESCRIPTION: After: P05-07. Done when: Keep its supported headed-under-Xvfb behavior and browser dependencies until parity is proven. Separate parser credentials, persistent reports/locks and execution limits; test container permissions, termination and dry-run mode.

CONTENT: [P05-09] Create readiness, liveness and migration contracts
DESCRIPTION: After: P05-08. Done when: Add safe liveness and dependency-aware readiness without credential leaks. Migrations must be backed up, idempotent and serialized; one elected migration runner must protect multi-instance/cloud startup.

CONTENT: [P05-10] Publish verified immutable images
DESCRIPTION: After: P05-09. Done when: After merged-main checks pass, build app/parser images once, scan them, record SBOM/provenance and publish commit tags plus digests. Smoke-test those exact images with disposable services before updating a deployable release manifest.

CONTENT: [P05-11] Add a versioned production deployment bundle
DESCRIPTION: After: P05-10. Done when: Check in Compose/runtime templates, example non-secret configuration, a release manifest and deployment/rollback scripts. Record image digests and supported schema versions; provide first-install and upgrade instructions.

CONTENT: [P05-12] GATE - rehearse install, restart, upgrade and restore
DESCRIPTION: After: P05-11. Done when: In a disposable environment, prove deep links, Auth0 configuration, private images, uploads, migrations, SIGTERM and data persistence across container replacement. App and parser must run without the working tree.

CONTENT: 06 - Private NAS production deployment
DESCRIPTION: Exit gate: one private NAS production deployment can safely update and roll back a tested release.

CONTENT: [P06-01] Prepare NAS folders and service permissions
DESCRIPTION: After: P05-12. Done when: Create separate restricted directories for configuration, media, database, reports, logs, release manifests and backups. Record numeric ownership, quota/free-space checks and an off-NAS encrypted backup destination.

CONTENT: [P06-02] Configure private container networking
DESCRIPTION: After: P06-01. Done when: Use a bridge network with internal service names. Expose only the application through the NAS reverse proxy; do not publish MongoDB, the API administration surface or DSM to the internet. Verify actual firewall rules.

CONTENT: [P06-03] Set up a stable HTTPS NAS application address
DESCRIPTION: After: P06-02. Done when: Configure LAN/VPN DNS, reverse proxy and trusted TLS. Choose an internal CA installed on reviewer devices or a valid domain/certificate approach without opening NAS inbound internet access. Never disable HTTPS/auth validation to make login work.

CONTENT: [P06-04] Configure production Auth0 and database credentials
DESCRIPTION: After: P06-03. Done when: Register exact NAS callback/logout/web origins, verify refresh behavior and preserve existing issuer/sub account identity. Use separate least-privilege app/parser DB users and keep secrets outside Git/images.

CONTENT: [P06-05] Back up and deploy the first tested release
DESCRIPTION: After: P06-04. Done when: Capture consistent DB plus media/metadata backups, restore-test them, install the versioned bundle and pull the approved digests. Verify migrations, readiness, guest operation and editor access before enabling normal writes.

CONTENT: [P06-06] Implement a NAS-initiated deployment job
DESCRIPTION: After: P06-05. Done when: DSM Task Scheduler or an equivalent local service polls a trusted release manifest, verifies approved SHA/digests, takes an exclusive deploy lock, pulls images and runs health checks. Hosted CI never needs inbound SSH access to the LAN.

CONTENT: [P06-07] Add safe deployment controls and rollback
DESCRIPTION: After: P06-06. Done when: Provide deploy-latest-tested, deploy-specific-release and rollback commands. Retain previous images/config; on failed app health restore the compatible previous image, not an automatic destructive DB restore. Record deployment logs and status.

CONTENT: [P06-08] Protect first releases and schema changes
DESCRIPTION: After: P06-07. Done when: Allow main merges automatically, but require an explicit promotion approval for the first NAS release and migrations with data impact. Enable unattended routine deployments only after rollback and compatibility evidence are recorded.

CONTENT: [P06-09] Exercise restart, outage and backup recovery
DESCRIPTION: After: P06-08. Done when: Reboot NAS/containers, simulate DB outage and failed image start, and verify graceful recovery. Restore DB and uploaded media together to an isolated target and compare counts/checksums against RPO/RTO.

CONTENT: [P06-10] GATE - approve private NAS production
DESCRIPTION: After: P06-09. Done when: Confirm a real LAN client can log in, navigate, edit, upload and persist progress, and an unauthorized network cannot reach the service. A failed release must leave a usable previous deployment.

CONTENT: 07 - Scheduled parser operations
DESCRIPTION: Exit gate: scheduled imports are repeatable, observable and preserve existing user and shared data.

CONTENT: [P07-01] Review the supported parser profiles
DESCRIPTION: After: P06-10. Done when: Confirm the current eight profiles: Endfield, Genshin, HSR, Wuthering Waves, ZZZ, Fate/Grand Order, Girls Frontline 2 and Neverness to Everness. Exclude FFXIV deliberately; do not reuse obsolete unsupported-game checklists.

CONTENT: [P07-02] Document parser inputs, time rules and expected outputs
DESCRIPTION: After: P07-01. Done when: Record current-version sources, dynamic-event sources and recurring daily/weekly/monthly/endgame definitions per game. Verify next-two-month coverage, local calendar-day handling and server reset rules with fixed-clock fixtures.

CONTENT: [P07-03] Run a containerized preview against protected credentials
DESCRIPTION: After: P07-02. Done when: Execute parser:preview with --report and per-game filters as needed. Inspect proposed changes without writes, source failures and data-loss risks; verify existing permanent/dynamic history and completion IDs are preserved.

CONTENT: [P07-04] Establish one active scheduler and lock
DESCRIPTION: After: P07-03. Done when: Use a persistent lock for NAS execution and prevent overlapping manual/scheduled jobs. Before any cross-host scheduling, add a durable shared lease or disable the other scheduler; filesystem locks do not coordinate separate hosts.

CONTENT: [P07-05] Create the Monday NAS scheduled task
DESCRIPTION: After: P07-04. Done when: Use DSM Task Scheduler at Monday 06:00 America/New_York, equivalent to 0 6 * * 1 in that scheduler timezone. Run the pinned parser image's parser:weekly command with --months=2 and a unique report path; verify DST behavior.

CONTENT: [P07-06] Set runtime, source pacing and failure policy
DESCRIPTION: After: P07-05. Done when: Preserve the existing 10-30 second navigation pacing and 10-second parse wait where needed. Bound total runtime/retries; report Cloudflare blocks and partial source failures distinctly. Never treat a blocked source as an empty dataset to delete.

CONTENT: [P07-07] Monitor reports and send failure alerts
DESCRIPTION: After: P07-06. Done when: Persist timestamped reports, latest summary, exit status, run duration, source freshness and counts of inserted/updated/skipped records. Notify the operator on partial/failed/missed runs; redact URLs containing credentials.

CONTENT: [P07-08] Test replay, manual recovery and parser rollback
DESCRIPTION: After: P07-07. Done when: Run one approved live import after a backup, repeat it to prove idempotency, interrupt a run to verify lock recovery and test per-game retry. Retain valid partial results; historical events and player completion remain intact.

CONTENT: [P07-09] Verify coverage in the actual events UI
DESCRIPTION: After: P07-08. Done when: Check Today/List/Calendar, type filters, Balance events and month boundaries for all eight games. Confirm daily tasks appear on intended days, reset cycles remain separate and expiring events sort correctly.

CONTENT: [P07-10] GATE - approve unattended parser scheduling
DESCRIPTION: After: P07-09. Done when: Record one successful scheduled run plus a controlled failure/alert and safe retry. Confirm the next Monday run, two-month horizon, backups and sole active writer before leaving automation enabled.

CONTENT: 08 - Private friend review and release candidate
DESCRIPTION: Exit gate: normal users validate the real deployment and release-blocking feedback is resolved.

CONTENT: [P08-01] Set up private reviewer connectivity
DESCRIPTION: After: P07-10. Done when: Use a limited VPN/device-sharing arrangement such as Tailscale, or trusted LAN access. Grant only the application service; deny DSM, SSH, MongoDB and unrelated NAS shares. Verify HTTPS and the selected Auth0 origin on a friend's device.

CONTENT: [P08-02] Create a reviewer onboarding checklist
DESCRIPTION: After: P08-01. Done when: Explain sign-in, private-beta scope, test games, known limitations, feedback location and how to revoke access. Use individual accounts; friends are ordinary users unless editor access is explicitly required.

CONTENT: [P08-03] Prepare safe review data and permissions
DESCRIPTION: After: P08-02. Done when: Keep private/unreleased games editor-only, separate test progress per account and avoid sharing your credentials. Review media and personal information before granting access; document whether beta data will carry into public launch.

CONTENT: [P08-04] Run the friend acceptance script
DESCRIPTION: After: P08-03. Done when: Ask reviewers to switch games, follow story deep links, track completion across refresh/tabs, manage characters/inventory, filter/balance events, upload only when authorized and sign out. Include mobile and keyboard use.

CONTENT: [P08-05] Validate account isolation and editor boundaries
DESCRIPTION: After: P08-04. Done when: Verify one reviewer cannot read another account's progress or perform editor actions. Test direct requests and restricted content/media access as well as hidden UI controls.

CONTENT: [P08-06] Collect, prioritize and fix beta findings
DESCRIPTION: After: P08-05. Done when: Triage reports using deployed version, severity and reproduction steps. Resolve data loss, access leaks, login failures and incorrect completion first; publish known nonblocking issues and retest fixes on the NAS.

CONTENT: [P08-07] Measure the deployment under realistic usage
DESCRIPTION: After: P08-06. Done when: Check initial/deep-link loads, event-list rendering, memory, API latency, concurrency, storage growth and parser impact. Set practical launch thresholds from evidence instead of invented capacity claims.

CONTENT: [P08-08] GATE - sign off the cloud release candidate
DESCRIPTION: After: P08-07. Done when: Have at least one friend complete the acceptance flow, confirm blockers are closed, prove access revocation and record the tested release digest. Private-beta signoff does not automatically publish the NAS.

CONTENT: 09 - Managed database migration
DESCRIPTION: Exit gate: the private NAS application and parser use a backed-up managed database without lost data.

CONTENT: [P09-01] Provision the chosen managed MongoDB service
DESCRIPTION: After: P08-08. Done when: Use the approved provider/region and production tier. Verify actual source/target MongoDB and driver compatibility, storage limits, backup/restore capabilities, cost alerts and separate administrative ownership.

CONTENT: [P09-02] Create app, parser and migration database roles
DESCRIPTION: After: P09-01. Done when: Use distinct credentials scoped to required databases/collections; avoid root/admin users in normal app/parser runtime. Enable provider-account MFA and store credentials only in approved secret stores.

CONTENT: [P09-03] Restrict Atlas network access and require TLS
DESCRIPTION: After: P09-02. Done when: Allow only confirmed NAS egress and later hosting egress/private networking. Plan for changing residential IPs; do not default to 0.0.0.0/0. Validate TLS/SRV/DNS connectivity without printing a connection string.

CONTENT: [P09-04] Rehearse a complete migration in an isolated database
DESCRIPTION: After: P09-03. Done when: Use an encrypted consistent dump/restore with compatible tools. Include shared catalogs, game rules, account/player progress, schema backups and indexes; separately verify uploaded file/metadata backups. Compare IDs, types, counts and sample references.

CONTENT: [P09-05] Schedule and announce a short write freeze
DESCRIPTION: After: P09-04. Done when: Choose a maintenance window and cutover owner. Pause the parser and all old app writers, drain in-flight work and take final database plus media manifests/backups. No standalone dump is assumed consistent while writes continue.

CONTENT: [P09-06] Restore the final dataset and switch NAS configuration
DESCRIPTION: After: P09-05. Done when: Restore into the managed target, verify indexes and integrity, update only DB secrets/config and start one application writer. Preserve Auth0 issuer/sub mapping, game/character/event IDs and completion records.

CONTENT: [P09-07] Validate production against the managed database
DESCRIPTION: After: P09-06. Done when: Check guest/editor/user permissions, story completion, character collections, inventory, image references, concurrency and one controlled parser run. Confirm no old local writers remain connected.

CONTENT: [P09-08] Enable tested backups and recovery monitoring
DESCRIPTION: After: P09-07. Done when: Set automated backup retention, encrypt an independent export as appropriate and restore to an isolated target. Monitor connectivity, capacity, long-lived catalog document size and account/progress writes.

CONTENT: [P09-09] Document a non-destructive cutover rollback
DESCRIPTION: After: P09-08. Done when: Before writes resume, reverting the connection is straightforward. After new writes exist, keep the managed DB authoritative or reconcile them deliberately; never point back to a stale local snapshot and silently lose user progress.

CONTENT: [P09-10] GATE - accept the managed database
DESCRIPTION: After: P09-09. Done when: Record integrity checks, one restore drill and successful NAS operation for an agreed observation period. Retain the old DB as a restricted recovery copy, with its parser/app writers disabled.

CONTENT: 10 - Public hosting and automated deployment
DESCRIPTION: Exit gate: a tested release is deployed to the public host with durable data and controlled promotion.

CONTENT: [P10-01] Provision the approved cloud application service
DESCRIPTION: After: P09-10. Done when: Create a Docker web service in the chosen region with budget/usage alerts and least-privilege provider accounts. Restrict reviewer access until launch and keep this inactive replacement from accepting competing production writes. Verify the tested image's PORT, health checks and limits.

CONTENT: [P10-02] Finish durable cloud media migration
DESCRIPTION: After: P10-01. Done when: Copy uploaded media and metadata to the approved storage adapter, compare checksums and preserve existing API references. Restart/redeploy the service to prove images survive; do not rely on ephemeral container disk.

CONTENT: [P10-03] Configure production secrets and network policies
DESCRIPTION: After: P10-02. Done when: Store DB/Auth0/storage values in provider secrets, restrict object-store permissions and allow the service's actual outbound network in Atlas. Deploy no root DB user or SPA client secret.

CONTENT: [P10-04] Configure domain, HTTPS and authentication
DESCRIPTION: After: P10-03. Done when: Set the final domain, DNS, TLS and exact Auth0 callbacks/logout/web origins. Preserve existing account identities, verify refresh/logout and reject mismatched tokens; test deep links and private image access under the final origin.

CONTENT: [P10-05] Automate digest-specific cloud promotion
DESCRIPTION: After: P10-04. Done when: After all checks and image smoke tests pass for merged main, deploy the approved image digest through the provider API. Verify the deployment reports the expected SHA; disable any competing deploy-on-push path that can skip the gate.

CONTENT: [P10-06] Add deployment concurrency and rollback controls
DESCRIPTION: After: P10-05. Done when: Serialize releases, hold migrations with data impact for approval, poll health and run a post-deploy smoke. On failure restore the previous compatible image and alert; record the last known good digest and keep deployment credentials secret.

CONTENT: [P10-07] Choose the final parser execution location
DESCRIPTION: After: P10-06. Done when: Prefer a managed scheduled container if cost/browser/network tests pass; otherwise retain NAS scheduling against the managed DB with monitoring. Record the single authoritative scheduler and avoid a second active writer.

CONTENT: [P10-08] Cut parser scheduling over safely if moving it
DESCRIPTION: After: P10-07. Done when: Stop the NAS job first. Make leases/reports durable in MongoDB/object storage, run the exact parser image and preserve --months=2. For Render UTC cron, choose 11:00 Monday UTC for 06:00 New York standard time and 10:00 UTC during daylight time, or use a timezone-aware scheduler.

CONTENT: [P10-09] Move active production traffic to cloud hosting
DESCRIPTION: After: P10-08. Done when: Freeze writes briefly if needed, verify cloud health, then switch the canonical application URL and retire the NAS web writer. Keep NAS private as a compatible recovery target; both recovery configuration and bookmarks must point to the authoritative managed DB.

CONTENT: [P10-10] GATE - rehearse a public-host release and rollback
DESCRIPTION: After: P10-09. Done when: Verify one automated release, a failed rollout, a rollback, persisted uploads/progress and scheduled parser recovery. The final SHA/digest must match CI evidence and no NAS port forwarding should be required.

CONTENT: 11 - Public go-live readiness and operations
DESCRIPTION: Exit gate: the application is safe to publish, supportable and recoverable.

CONTENT: [P11-01] Complete a public security review
DESCRIPTION: After: P10-10. Done when: Review access control, account isolation, upload/file validation, unsafe Markdown/XSS, request limits, CORS, proxy headers, CSP and other security headers. Address findings with regression tests; do not mistake passing CI for a full security assessment.

CONTENT: [P11-02] Verify secrets and administrative access
DESCRIPTION: After: P11-01. Done when: Scan source/history/images and public diagnostics, rotate any exposed or obsolete credentials, enforce MFA and least privilege, and document emergency revocation. Remove unused NAS/cloud/Auth0 permissions and temporary DB access-list entries.

CONTENT: [P11-03] Publish privacy, support and content policies
DESCRIPTION: After: P11-02. Done when: Explain personal data, auth/storage providers, feedback retention, account deletion/export and support contacts. Review licensed artwork/source attribution and visibility before publication; obtain appropriate policy/legal review for the intended audience.

CONTENT: [P11-04] Exercise data export and deletion
DESCRIPTION: After: P11-03. Done when: Verify users can recover/export intended personal data and request or perform deletion. Ensure deletion removes the correct account's progress/feedback without deleting shared game data; document backups and retention exceptions.

CONTENT: [P11-05] Check accessibility and essential browser journeys
DESCRIPTION: After: P11-04. Done when: Verify keyboard focus, screen-reader labels, dropdowns, contrast, reduced motion, responsive layouts, 404/error recovery, empty/loading states and expired-login recovery. Confirm game navigation and shared links work without a developer session.

CONTENT: [P11-06] Configure monitoring and actionable alerts
DESCRIPTION: After: P11-05. Done when: Monitor readiness, error rates, slow requests, DB/storage capacity, certificate expiry, failed deploys, stale parser data and missed backups. Set an accountable alert destination and remove tokens/PII from logs.

CONTENT: [P11-07] Practice incidents and database/media restoration
DESCRIPTION: After: P11-06. Done when: Rehearse bad release, auth failure, provider outage, corrupt upload and parser failure. Restore into an isolated target, measure RPO/RTO and document when to roll back code versus restore data or fix forward.

CONTENT: [P11-08] Create recurring operating checklists
DESCRIPTION: After: P11-07. Done when: Assign weekly failed-job/feedback review, monthly dependency and cost review, periodic access review and restore drills. Track renewal dates and backup retention; create recurring Todoist tasks separately once owners/cadence are agreed.

CONTENT: [P11-09] GATE - approve public launch
DESCRIPTION: After: P11-08. Done when: Require P01-09, P02-08, P03-10, P04-08, P05-12, P06-10, P07-10, P08-08, P09-10, P10-10 and the tasks in this phase. Publish only reviewed games/features, with no unresolved access/data-loss blockers and a named rollback owner.

CONTENT: 12 - Launch, promotion and portfolio
DESCRIPTION: Exit gate: the public launch is verified and the portfolio describes evidence-backed work.

CONTENT: [P12-01] Publish the first public release
DESCRIPTION: After: P11-09. Done when: Tag the tested release, publish reviewed changelog notes, confirm domain/login/guest paths from an external network and watch errors, usage and costs during the initial launch window. Announce only after the launch gate passes.

CONTENT: [P12-02] Perform post-launch acceptance and feedback review
DESCRIPTION: After: P12-01. Done when: Check real user sign-in, account isolation, event freshness, saved progress and image delivery after launch. Review early feedback and execute the rollback plan if a release blocker appears.

CONTENT: [P12-03] Prepare a public project landing page and README
DESCRIPTION: After: P12-02. Done when: Explain the product, supported games/features, screenshots, live URL, setup boundaries and contribution/support process. Keep credentials, internal NAS details and private-user data out of examples.

CONTENT: [P12-04] Create a portfolio case study
DESCRIPTION: After: P12-03. Done when: Describe Angular/TypeScript UI, shared-data versus personal-progress design, Auth0 authorization, CI/browser tests, parser scheduling, Docker/NAS and managed-cloud delivery. Include architecture, tradeoffs and measured results with redacted screenshots.

CONTENT: [P12-05] Add accurate resume and profile entries
DESCRIPTION: After: P12-04. Done when: Summarize your own engineering and product decisions, describe AI-assisted development candidly and link the live demo/repository where appropriate. Use only verified user, coverage, performance or reliability metrics; do not invent scale.

CONTENT: [P12-06] Prepare promotion materials and a safe demo
DESCRIPTION: After: P12-05. Done when: Create a short walkthrough and guest/demo path that cannot alter another user's data. Verify screenshot/media permissions, label beta limits and choose relevant communities whose promotion rules permit the post.

CONTENT: [P12-07] Publish announcements and collect results
DESCRIPTION: After: P12-06. Done when: After reviewing the final text yourself, share through selected personal/professional/community channels. Track useful feedback, engagement and conversion without invasive analytics; do not post automatically as part of a code deployment.

CONTENT: [P12-08] Review the first month and prioritize improvements
DESCRIPTION: After: P12-07. Done when: Compare support issues, parser freshness, cost, reliability and real usage against launch targets. Update the roadmap, recurring maintenance tasks and portfolio evidence; remove unused infrastructure.
